Handoff state. Implemented and pushed as Gerrit change 2530 ("Partition ticket types"). Gate state at handoff: LLM-Review +1, Verified -1 — the code review PASSED and only CI is red.

Two failure signatures are open across this stack and neither root cause is confirmed yet:
1. change 2530 fails the `require resolvable rebar ticket` job, although `rebar resolve` succeeds locally and the trailer is well-formed — the leading hypothesis is that the ticket is not visible to CI (the `tickets` branch may not have reached `origin`);
2. pytest fails in ~50s on several changes, fast enough to be a collection/import error, and it does NOT reproduce locally.

Do NOT close this ticket until its change is Verified +1 and merged. A subagent is driving the stack to green; a session-only cron loop (46e3b0eb) is harvesting reviews, landing green changes and closing merged tickets.

Note for whoever lands this: amend only with `git commit --amend --no-edit`. Re-committing a change that already carries a Change-Id opens a DUPLICATE Gerrit change — that is how change 2534 came to exist and be abandoned.

Cross-session diagnosis from the debug-orchestrator session (I do not own this ticket; flagging because my orphan bug 3a02-66ea-9229-470c is blocked behind this stack).

## The whole six-change stack is red because of THIS change

Gerrit stack topology (via /revisions/current/related): 2530 -> 2531 -> 2533 -> 2535 -> 2536 -> 2537, one linear chain with 2530 at the base. All six carry LLM-Review +1 / Verified -1. Five of them have NO independent code defect; they inherit 2530's tree.

## Root cause

This ticket's recorded file_impact names `src/rebar/types.py` as the 'canonical home: declares the plan-review exemption and derives its complement beside TicketType'. But `src/rebar/types.py` is a GENERATED file. Its own header says so verbatim:

    Typed return contract for the public rebar.* facade — GENERATED.
    DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Regenerate with::
        python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types

Change 2530 patch set 2 adds `get_args` to its typing import plus the `PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES` constant and its complement. The CI drift gate regenerates the file from the canonical JSON Schemas and diffs it; regeneration DROPS the hand-written lines, so the gate fails with:

    src/rebar/types.py is stale — regenerate it with python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types

Evidence it is inherited rather than independent: change 2533's pytest job (run 100440611432) prints that exact removal diff, and 2533 touches no types.py of its own. The same error appears verbatim on 2535, 2536, 2537.

## Also worth noting

The LLM-Review bot DID flag this on patch set 2, correctly and in terms matching the CI failure ('src/rebar/types.py ... is a fully GENERATED file ... will fail the drift-gate unit test'), but classified it ADVISORY (non-blocking) — so the change still carries +1. A finding that provably reds the build is arguably blocking-severity; that severity-classification gap may deserve its own ticket.

## Earlier layer, already fixed

Patch set 1 of 2530/2531 (~21:07-21:15 UTC) failed a DIFFERENT shared gate: the 800-LOC module-size cap, at `804 src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`. Patch set 2 trimmed composer.py by 13 lines and cleared it, which is what exposed the types.py drift underneath.

## Environmental layer on top (2530 and 2531 only)

Patch set 2 of 2530 and 2531 never reached pytest at all — their runs died in the 'require resolvable rebar ticket' job at `git fetch` of refs/changes/... with HTTP 504 after a 60s hang, i.e. the Gerrit host failing to serve a packfile. That is provably environmental and a recheck is legitimate FOR THE 504. But a recheck alone will not turn either green: once the fetch succeeds they hit the same types.py drift gate their descendants already demonstrate. Timestamps ~21:57-21:59 UTC (14:57-14:59 PDT) fall OUTSIDE the 02:05-07:10 PDT root-disk outage window, so this is a later hiccup or that outage's tail — I could not determine which.

## What unblocks the stack

Fix 2530 only: the exemption constants need a hand-written home (or the generator must emit them). Then 2531 and the rest should go green on a rebase.

compiled_state.description:
Mirror inventory finding F3 (`reports/stability/mirror-inventory.md`), HIGH, comments already drifted.

## Problem

Which ticket types the plan-review gate reviews is one fact with SIX masters, and nothing
asserts they partition `TicketType`:

**Exempt** — `("bug", "session_log", "code_review", "identity")`
- `_commands/gates.py:45` `_PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES` (start-work gate)
- `_commands/composer.py:47` `_FILE_IMPACT_EXEMPT_TYPES` (create-time file-impact nudge)
- `llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:560` — inline literal

**Complement** — `("task", "story", "epic")`
- `llm/plan_review/claimability.py:38` `_REVIEWED_TYPES`
- `_commands/transition_close.py:46` `_PLAN_REVIEW_CLOSE_TYPES`
- `_commands/gates.py:215` — inline literal

`TicketType` (`types.py:23`) has exactly seven members, so 4 + 3 partitions it TODAY. The defect
is that nothing holds it that way: an eighth type lands in NEITHER set and is then neither gated
nor exempted. This decides whether the plan-review claim gate runs at all.

The single-sourcing claims are false, and one is drifted beyond being merely optimistic:
- `gates.py:42-44` — "Single-sourced here so ... cannot drift". It is not; five other sites exist.
- `composer.py:42-46` — admits "Kept in lockstep with", and MISDESCRIBES its counterpart: it cites
  the orchestrator as a "bug/session_log short-circuit before P9", but `orchestrator.py:560` sits
  inside the attestation DRIFT-REFRESH candidate path, not P9. Verified by reading the enclosing
  docstring.
- `claimability.py:40-41` prose names 2 of the 4 exempt types.

The only test is `assert "bug" in ...` (`test_bug_blast_radius_escalation_ad0d.py:199`).

## Approach — single-source the pair, then assert the partition

`types.py` already owns `TicketType` and is a true leaf (its only import is `typing`), so it is
the canonical home. Declare the exemption there and DERIVE its complement, so the two can never
disagree:

    PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES = frozenset({"bug", "session_log", "code_review", "identity"})
    PLAN_REVIEW_REVIEWED_TYPES = frozenset(get_args(TicketType)) - PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES

Then point all six sites at them.

**On epic AC2 (do not collapse a distinct concept).** The six sites serve four consumers — the
start-work gate, the create-time file-impact nudge, drift-refresh applicability, and the close
gate. They are not four different rules; they are four consumers of ONE predicate: "is this a
type whose plan the plan-review gate reviews?" Drift-refresh refreshes a plan-review
ATTESTATION, which only exists for reviewed types, so it is the same question. `composer`'s own
comment states the lockstep intent explicitly, so referencing one constant is faithful to the
author's intent rather than a merge of unrelated sets. If a consumer ever needs to diverge, that
becomes an explicit reviewed change instead of silent drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: `types.py` declares the exemption and derives the complement, and a test asserts the
      two are disjoint and their union is exactly `set(get_args(TicketType))`. Verified by that
      test failing if a member is added to `TicketType` without being placed in either set.
- [x] AC2: all six sites reference the canonical constants; no ticket-type literal tuple remains
      at any of them. Verified by a test that greps the six modules for a re-listed exempt or
      reviewed tuple and finds none.
- [x] AC3: adding a hypothetical eighth `TicketType` member fails the partition test rather than
      silently defaulting. Verified by the test parameterizing over an extended member set.
- [x] AC4: the three false/drifted comments are corrected — `gates.py`'s "cannot drift" claim,
      `composer.py`'s misdescription of `orchestrator.py:560` as a P9 short-circuit, and
      `claimability.py`'s partial enumeration. Verified by reading each against the code it cites.
- [x] AC5: behavior is unchanged for all seven current types. Verified by the existing gate and
      close-gate suites passing untouched, and by a test asserting the resolved exempt/reviewed
      sets equal the literals the six sites carried before this change.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "ticket_type or plan_review_exempt or partition" -q` — the
  partition, no-literals, and eighth-type tests (AC1, AC2, AC3).
- `python -m pytest tests/unit -q` — proves the six call sites still gate identically (AC5); these
  constants sit on the claim and close paths, so a mistake here is broad and loud.
- `make lint && make typecheck`.
